Subject: Re: Fwd: Live chat - spike — triage notes

Acknowledged. Quick notes from initial triage (19:45):
- Grafana: saw clear p95/p99 uplift starting 18:05 PDT; concurrent connections increased by ~28% in BrightHelp's tenant.
- Autoscaling: no failed scale events; dedicated pool hit soft limit and we observed longer queue wait times for short sequences.
- Runtime traces: increased kernel time on attention for large context reuse; KV cache hit ratio dropped during the spike (likely due to a higher diversity of sessions), causing more full-attention passes.
- Errors: 500s are in the request deserialization path when socket read times out during prolonged backpressure (we're surfacing a downstream Nginx 502 in a small subset).

Proposed mitigations (fast):
1) Roll traffic for BrightHelp to previous model variant (v1.14) which has lower memory/KV churn and tested better under connection churn. This is a config-only change; can be applied in 2–4 minutes with routing policy.
2) Short-term: bump soft concurrency limit for BrightHelp's dedicated slot to reduce queuing.
3) Medium: enable prefix/KV aggressive caching profile for this tenant for evening windows.

I'll prepare a runbook and start the rollback if we get customer sign-off. Pasting quick links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming/latency?from=2028-06-18T18:00:00Z&to=2028-06-18T22:00:00Z

—Rishi
SRE Lead, Redwood Serving Runtime

Date: 2028-06-18T21:10:00-07:00
Subject: Exec note: BrightHelp evening tail-latency incident — summary + ask

Naomi — quick executive summary for visibility:
- Impact: BrightHelp observed a streaming chat p95 regression to ~1.1s and p99 >3s from ~18:05–19:20 PDT, with throughput degraded ~30% and ~0.8% elevated 500s surfaced to the customer. User experience: reconnects and some dropped messages.
- Cause (initial triage): higher session-length diversity and elevated long-sequence fraction caused KV cache churn and longer attention kernel time; queuing/backpressure exposed a small downstream proxy timeout in a subset of hosts.
- Immediate actions taken: routing rollback to model v1.14 executed at 20:18 PDT; temporary bump to soft concurrency for BrightHelp; 20:15–20:40 bridge completed with BrightHelp and validated reduced tail latency.
- Customer ask: short SLA credit (evening peak) and a formal post-incident follow-up (root cause + mitigation timeline).

Request: please advise on credit authorization for this mid-sized account (DEAL-3019). Evelyn and I have a proposed credit figure (1 day pro-rata) pending your approval; we also request prioritization on the caching/kv mitigation change (estimated 2 sprints).

I will send a full postmortem draft by tomorrow morning with dashboards, timeline, and action items.

—Marissa

- Impact: p95/p99 returned to baseline after rollback; throughput recovered and 500s dropped to baseline. BrightHelp confirmed reduced reconnects during monitored window.
- Actions completed: rollback + concurrency bump + bridge validated mitigations.

  * Evelyn: customer-facing postmortem and proposed credit (1 day pro-rata) to send by EOD 2028-06-19.
  * Marissa: follow up on contract/credit approval with Naomi and record in HubSpot (DEAL-3019).

Customer comment from Alex: “Rollback fixed the evening tail behavior — appreciate the quick response.”
